newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up, led by brewing, industry giants. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up, led by brewing, industry giants. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects sectors responsible for rise in headline)

BOGOTA, June 11 Reuter - Colombian stocks edged up Wednesday by wafer-thin margins in sessions dominated by pocket-to-pocket cross deals in the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate and brewing giant Bavaria, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index ended up 0.19 percent to 1,181.59 amid a 1.7 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED index closed up 0.12 percent at 17,915.53 amid a 5.7 billion peso volume. "There's still a lot of buyers out there but as shareholders are looking to take profits buyers want hefty discounts," one Bogota broker said.
Volume on the Medellin exchange was concentrated on Bavaria which traded 1.56 billion pesos of stocks rising 0.19 percent to 7,755. In Bogota it closed up 0.07 percent at 7,756.
Other gainers included Cemento Argos, head of the cement producing arm of the Sindicato Antioqueno. It closed up 0.12 percent at 8,511 in Bogota and 0.13 percent up at the same price in Medellin.
One of the day's biggest fallers was insurance giant Suramericana de Seguros, flagship of the Sindicato Antioqueno. It fell 1.39 percent to 28,400 in Medellin and 1.03 percent to 28,600 in Bogota.
